title: A wheelchair user greeting a dog
description: Follow the approach, the pause, and the hand reaching down to greet the dog.
prompt: Cinematic, heartwarming style. On a sun-dappled park pathway in autumn, an elderly man with a kind, weathered face, dressed in a comfortable gray sweater, smoothly navigates in his electric wheelchair. The man gently halts his wheelchair, a warm smile spreading across his face as he reaches down to affectionately scratch the dog behind its ears. The scene is shot with a shallow depth of field and bathed in warm, golden lighting.

title: Inspecting a split keyboard
description: Compare the keyboard structure, its adjustment, and the requested diagram and badge.
prompt:
A bright studio workspace features an ergonomic split keyboard with two angled halves and a central module. A designer uses a small hex tool to adjust the key module positions, while a writer sits across and types a long passage. The keyboard base has an engraved badge. A tablet mounted on a stand shows a layout diagram of the keyboard with annotations and a measurement readout. On the desk, a configuration card lists the keyboard's ergonomic settings and warranty details. Text on keyboard badge (engraved) reads exactly: "SPLITFORM PRO
Adjustable split keyboard with ergonomic angles". Text on tablet screen reads exactly: "Tenting angle: 12° / Module gap: 2.1 cm / Scan: READY
Rotation: 15° vertical offset. Thumb cluster: adjustable.
Hex tool adjusts module gap and tent. Measurement shown in mm.". Text on configuration card reads exactly: "ErgoPreset 9: 30° tenting, 0° tilt, low actuation. Warranty: 2-year coverage on switches and electronics.
Keys: 74. Hotswap switches. Connectivity: USB-C and RF.
Set-to mode: Use hex tool to match your shoulder width and forearm angle. Gap 1-5 cm, tent 0-30°. Electrical contacts hidden under magnetic cover. Charge lasts 60 days.". The designer turns the hex tool to change the angle between the two keyboard halves. As the writer types, the designer points to the tablet screen, then lifts the keyboard to show the badge to the camera. The writer continues typing while the designer reads the configuration card aloud.

title: Notes, a tracklist, and a cassette
description: Follow the tabletop objects through the conversation and cassette interaction.
prompt: Two old friends sit at a kitchen table with a cassette deck, a typewritten liner note, an open spiral notebook full of song titles, a faded postcard, and a newer index card. A half-empty mug and a pen lie between them; the deck door is open and a cassette sits on the table. Text on typewritten J-card liner note reads exactly: "Lake House, 1994. The lake kept every wrong turn. You hid the oars because you were not ready to leave. I called it a lie, so you mailed me the date I refused. Play side B loud. The hiss is the water we almost lost.". Text on handwritten tracklist in spiral notebook reads exactly: "Side A: Salt on the Porch — we cracked the porch light; The Bee Line; Lantern Logic. Side B: Almost-Float; The Postcard That Lied — because the date was wrong.". Text on faded postcard reads exactly: "August 1 — I hid the oars. Not gone. Love, Lena". Text on new index-card note reads exactly: "Found the oars under the porch. The card was sent July 30 but dated Aug. 1.". Mira turns the postcard over and taps the postmark, then slides the index card to Lena. Lena reads it, compares the tracklist's last song title with the postcard, and pencils the true postmark date onto the back of the postcard. The cassette begins to play, and the two friends lean toward the speaker without speaking.
